claim.why_it_matters: The 20-21 row of the WHEN-COMPILED returned-value table is no longer a table row, so any tool or reader consuming the 15.99.3 table sees only positions 1 through 19 and the last two character positions of the 21-character returned value fall out of the structure. The transcription already has the correct convention for this exact situation — the identical CURRENT-DATE table split across pages 864/865 restarts with a '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' header row and continues the table — so page 968 is an inconsistent degradation, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED as a content discrepancy; it is page-break/table-markup formatting only. (1) Text presence: I rendered PDF page 968 (printed folio 938) at 300 dpi and read it. The page carries exactly three blocks: the '20-21 ...' row, rule 2), and rule 3). The markdown page-968 block in specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries the same three blocks in the same order, and the 20-21 sentence is word-for-word identical to the printed text, including the '20-21' position label, the range '00 through 59', the '+' / en-dash disjunction, and the trailing "If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned." Nothing is missing, nothing is moved out of its section, nothing is reworded, and no choice indicator or glyph is lost. The row is still adjacent to and immediately after the table it belongs to, still under 15.99.3 rule 1), and still before rule 2). The sole delta is that the line is a paragraph rather than a '| 20-21 | ... |' pipe-table row, i.e. markdown markup, not content. Meaning is unchanged: the position-to-contents mapping is preserved by the leading '20-21' label in both sources. (2) The claim's own supporting argument does not survive inspection. It asserts page 968 is an 'inconsistent degradation' versus the identical CURRENT-DATE split at 864/865, where the markdown restarts the table with a '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' header. I rendered PDF page 865 (folio 835) as well: that page REPRINTS the 'Character Positions / Contents' column headings above its 20-21 row. PDF page 968 does NOT reprint them — it opens directly with the bare '20-21' continuation row under the running head. So the two markdown pages are treated differently because the two PDF pages are genuinely printed differently; the transcription is tracking its source, not degrading arbitrarily. The claim omits this material fact and thereby misrepresents the comparison it rests on. (3) The 'kind' label is wrong on its face: nothing is misplaced. The content sits in exactly the position the PDF prints it. At most this is 'table not continued across a page break', which is precisely the page-break-furniture / formatting class the verification rules direct me to reject. Note for completeness, and not as support for this claim: the markdown renders the en-dash as U+FFFD ('�') here, but that mojibake is document-wide (it appears in the 18-19 and 17 rows on page 967 and in the CURRENT-DATE table on 864 too), is a separate encoding defect, and is not what was claimed.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. The full 20-21 row text of the 15.99.3 WHEN-COMPILED returned-value table is transcribed verbatim, in the right section and the right order, with its '20-21' label intact; it is merely emitted as a paragraph instead of being continued as a pipe-table row after the page-967/968 break. If the reconciliation wants machine-extractable tables, continuing the table on page 968 would be a cosmetic markup improvement (severity: cosmetic, kind: table-continuation-markup), but it is not lost, moved, or altered content, and it does not change meaning. The claim's premise that this is an inconsistency versus the 864/865 CURRENT-DATE split is itself incorrect: PDF page 865 reprints the 'Character Positions / Contents' column headings, whereas PDF page 968 does not, so the two markdown pages differ because the two source pages differ.
